title: The Bunker Under My Garden
summary: A woman built a small bunker while the street laughed. Tonight the street is at her hatch, and it only holds six.
inspired_by: https://youtu.be/eEv2AtJh0nM (premise only: the neighbours who laughed at the bunker now want in)

beats.text: They laughed at my garden bunker. Tonight eleven neighbours are knocking on its hatch.
It holds six. Food for six, air for six, and a hatch that locks from inside.
Mr. Pell knocked first. He laughed the loudest. He was not laughing now.
My rule, on the wall: let in what the air allows. Not one more.
I took the children first. Then their mothers. Then an old man and his dog.
Six places filled. Above us Pell asked softly, please.
I slid the lock across and sat against it. I did not answer.
By midnight the knocking stopped. The children slept. I called it kindness.
At two I counted us again. Six. Good. Six.
Then three slow knocks came from below the floor, where I never built a door.
